subject: Signer delegation & PO routing questions for Ariba enrollment (MSA + Order Form)
messages:
From: Anna Wells <anna.wells@hollowayhealth.com>
To: soojin.lee@redwood.com
Cc: procureops@hollowayhealth.com
Date: Tue, 7 Feb 2028 14:22:00 -0500
Subject: Clarify signer delegation + PO routing for Ariba enrollment (MSA redlines attached)

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for sending the draft MSA and order form. We're close, but procurement had two gating questions that block Ariba activation:

1) Signer delegation: our legal team asks that the MSA explicitly allow our procurement system to route POs signed on behalf of the company when signature authority has been delegated. The redline we received yesterday removed the explicit delegation language and procurement is asking us to confirm Redwood will accept PO transmissions that include a delegated signer token.

2) PO routing / acknowledgement: we need an explicit acceptance window and PO routing spec to ensure our EDI/Ariba acknowledgements match Redwood's PO-ack expectations. Attached is our PO routing spec and a sample PO that shows the fields we rely on (buyerId, siteId, poPrefix).

Can your legal or onboarding ops team confirm if the edits in the attached MSA (Redwood_MSA_edited_v3.docx) are acceptable or if you need alternate wording? If Redwood needs to preserve liability language that prevents delegated signers from binding the company, we need a short note we can share with our procurement stakeholders so they can decide whether to proceed with manual exceptions.

We'd like to keep the Ariba registration window open this week — can we get confirmation by end of day Thursday?

Thanks,
Anna

--
Anna Wells
Senior Procurement Manager
Holloway Health
anna.wells@hollowayhealth.com
procureops@hollowayhealth.com

Attachments: Redline_MSA_from_Holloway.docx (changes highlighted), Holloway_PO_Routing_Spec.xlsx

To: Anna Wells <anna.wells@hollowayhealth.com>

Date: Wed, 8 Feb 2028 09:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Clarify signer delegation + PO routing for Ariba enrollment (MSA redlines attached)

Thanks Anna — appreciate the clear summary and the spec. Quick note while I loop in Legal Ops and Procurement Ops: we can typically accept EDI/Ariba POs that are routed by an authorized procurement system even when a signer is delegated, provided the order form references the same acceptance terms and the MSA doesn't contain independent language invalidating delegated signers.

I'm forwarding to Kimberly (legal) and Markus (ops) to confirm the redline implications and to propose short alternative language that preserves Redwood's standard liability carveouts while allowing Holloway's delegated-signer workflow.

Sincerely,
Soojin Lee
Vendor Onboarding Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: Clarify signer delegation + PO routing for Ariba enrollment (MSA redlines attached)

Folks — forwarding Anna's note and Holloway's PO spec. I reviewed the Holloway redline and Redwood_MSA_edited_v3.docx. Short version: we can accept delegated-signature flows if the Order Form explicitly ties PO acceptance to the purchase token and the POs include a unique procurement-system identifier. We need three small edits:

1) Add a one-sentence acceptance clause to the Order Form: "Company accepts POs transmitted via Holloway Health's procurement system, provided each PO includes Holloway's procurement system identifier and is issued in accordance with the Order Form's terms."

2) In the MSA, preserve Redwood's limitation of liability paragraph but add a parenthetical: "(for the avoidance of doubt, delegated signers bound by an authorized procurement system identifier are treated as authorized agents for PO acceptance)."

3) Add a PO-ack window of 3 business days in the Order Form and reference the attached PO routing spec as the canonical field mapping doc.

I attached a tracked-change version (Redwood_MSA_edited_v3.docx) with the proposed language and a short redline of the Order Form. Markus, can you confirm operationally we can support buyerId/siteId mapping and the poPrefix normalization in the attached Excel? If yes, we'll push the two small edits to Anna and ask Holloway to sign the updated Order Form (DocuSign link below).

DocuSign (proposed envelope): https://www.docusign.com/envelope/987654321
Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aBcdExampleDoc

Thanks — Kimberly

--
Kimberly Park
Director, Legal Operations
Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Attachments: Redwood_MSA_edited_v3.docx (tracked changes), OrderForm_PO_Routing_Redline.docx

From: markus.klein@redwood.com
To: Anna Wells <anna.wells@hollowayhealth.com>, soojin.lee@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 10 Feb 2028 11:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Clarify signer delegation + PO routing for Ariba enrollment (MSA redlines attached)

Anna / team — quick operational confirmation. We can support Holloway's buyerId/siteId and poPrefix mapping. Implementation notes:

- We'll accept inbound Ariba POs that include Holloway's procurement system identifier in the buyerId field. We will map buyerId -> account, siteId -> delivery site, and strip any poPrefix for canonical PO number storage.
- PO acknowledgements (PO-ACK) will be sent within 3 business days after validation; missing required fields will trigger an "ACK with exception" message back to your procureops mailbox so you can remedy.
- For delegated-signature validation: if the procurement system token is present and matches our onboarding whitelist, we will treat the PO as binding. We will not accept POs that rely solely on a handwritten/printed signature image without procurement metadata.

Next steps:
1) Kimberly, final redline language for MSA + Order Form (one-sentence acceptance + parenthetical in limitation of liability) — once you confirm I'll route to DocuSign.
2) Anna, confirm Holloway agrees to the 3-business-day PO-ACK window and that your EDI team will include the procurement system identifier in buyerId for all vendor POs.

Markus Klein
Senior Manager, Serving Ops (Onboarding)
Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com
